name: UnsignedBytewiseOrd
documentation:
Marks that a type should be treated as an unsigned byte for comparisons.

 # Safety
 * The type must be readable as an `u8`, meaning it has to have the same
   layout as `u8` and always be initialized.
 * For every `x` and `y` of this type, `Ord(x, y)` must return the same
   value as `Ord::cmp(transmute::<_, u8>(x), transmute::<_, u8>(y))`.
rules: An implementor of `UnsignedBytewiseOrd` must have the same layout as `u8` and always be initialized, so that values of the type are readable as `u8`.
For every `x` and `y` of a type implementing `UnsignedBytewiseOrd`, `Ord(x, y)` must return the same value as `Ord::cmp(transmute::<_, u8>(x), transmute::<_, u8>(y))`.
